subject.title: Feature: TTS delivery mode option — separate text + voice messages on Telegram

question: Should OpenClaw add a public Telegram TTS delivery policy for separate text-plus-voice delivery, and should that policy live under global `messages.tts`, Telegram/channel config, or a channel capability?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the fix adds public config surface and overlaps with captioned-final and voice-only TTS directions, so automation should not choose the contract.

options.title: Approve a narrow delivery policy
options.body: Define a backward-compatible bundled/captioned versus separate mode, document it, and require Telegram unit tests plus live proof before implementation.

options.title: Standardize captioned delivery
options.body: Keep captioned voice as the supported Telegram default and document tagged/manual splitting plus overflow fallback instead of adding another config path.

options.title: Defer until captioned-final settles
options.body: Wait for the active captioned-final TTS PR direction before deciding whether separate delivery should become first-class.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow delivery policy
recommendation.body: Define a backward-compatible bundled/captioned versus separate mode, document it, and require Telegram unit tests plus live proof before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest feature-history signal across core TTS policy, public config, and Telegram caption delivery, which are the decision boundaries here.
